mainEntity.name: Why is photography an art of observation?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Photography involves choosing what deserves attention and

how to show it. The photographer notices light, gestures,

shapes and relationships, then uses viewpoint, framing and

timing to communicate what matters. Different photographers

can interpret the same scene in different ways.

mainEntity.name: How can I improve my observation skills in photography?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Spend time looking before you raise the camera. Notice the

light, explore the background and watch what changes.

Try the

ten-minute observation exercise ,

then compare what interested you with what appears in your

photograph. Choose one specific thing to practise next time.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between observation and composition?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Observation is noticing and interpreting what is happening

in a scene. Composition is choosing how to arrange what you

include within the photograph. Observation gives you a reason

to make the picture; composition helps you express that reason.

The two work together as you explore and refine your frame.

mainEntity.name: Should I always wait before taking a photograph?

acceptedAnswer.text:
No. Waiting can help you discover possibilities, but a fleeting

expression, movement or change in light may need an immediate

response. Keep your camera ready. Observation practice should

help you recognise when to act, and you can continue exploring

after capturing the moment.

mainEntity.name: Can I develop a photographic eye using a phone?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes. You can practise noticing light, choosing a viewpoint,

watching movement and checking the edges of your frame with

a phone. These decisions apply whatever camera you use.

Keep the camera app ready and reduce interruptions while

you observe.

mainEntity.name: What should I look for when a scene seems ordinary?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Look for a change in light, a reflection, a repeated shape,

a gesture or an unexpected relationship between subjects.

Try moving a little or changing your camera height.

An ordinary location can offer interesting details, although

you do not need to make a photograph every time you stop.

mainEntity.name: How does observation help with storytelling in photography?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Observation helps you notice the gestures, surroundings and

relationships that give a photograph context. Your timing

and framing determine which of those clues the viewer can

see. Explore this further in

The Art of Storytelling in Photography .

mainEntity.name: How do I know whether my observation led to a successful photograph?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Recall what caught your attention, then look at whether it

comes across clearly in the image. Check what competes with

it and whether your timing and viewpoint helped. The review

process in

Lesson 34

will help you assess those choices.
